context:
Goal: guards that block only real mistakes, so a refusal is never a false alarm you have to type override past.
Problem (rule): today every guard blocks from the day it ships, so a false alarm shows up only after it has cost a session, and the team's verification article uses a log-only stage first; this changes how guards ship, so it is your call.
Based on (read): the verification article (https://claude.dev/blog/how-the-claude-code-team-thinks-about-verification/): a gate with off, observe and enforce modes, and a let-through after two blocks in a session (triage read it through a page summary, not word for word).
Based on (ruling): outcomes-mechanize-rules in CLAUDE.md: watching must cost less than what it watches, and a log needs a named reader.
Departs from: main — every guard blocks from the day it ships — b adds a log-only stage for new guards.
Waiting on: nothing stopped; step guard-stages-observe is blocked until you pick.

lastAnswer.note: can we do keep guards blocking but maybe also star t logigng into potentially a review mode chjeck in on the review log?

options.gain: No new mode and no new log.
options.how: No change; false alarms are found by use and culled later.
options.label: Keep guards blocking from the first day
options.lose: A false alarm costs you before anyone sees it.

options.gain: The false-alarm rate is known before a guard blocks.
options.how: A new guard logs what it would have blocked, read on demand by the session that built it, and starts blocking after a named reading; no let-through.
options.label: New guards run log-only first, then block
options.lose: A new guard does not block at first; a log with a named reader to keep.

options.gain: A session is never stuck on a wrong guard.
options.how: As b, and a session is let through after two refusals of the same guard so it is never stuck.
options.label: Log-only stage and a let-through after two blocks
options.lose: A mistaken act passes after two refusals, which is the act a guard exists to stop.

options.gain: Guards keep blocking from the first day, and a named reader finds false alarms, with no new process.
options.how: No stage change. Each refusal is already written to the guard log, which lint/guard_log_report.py reads; triage reads it at each roadmap review and files each false alarm as a debt or a guard fix. In a cloud session that report reads n/a, so the first act is to find where the log lives for a cloud container.
options.label: Keep guards blocking, and read the guard log on a schedule (recommended)
options.lose: A false alarm still blocks once before it is seen; whether cloud sessions write a readable log is unmeasured.

ref: owner chat 19:45 CST Nov 17 (relayed by the consultant): review the two blogs and land their findings
reply: Read at 20:10 CST Nov 17 by triage 11; still open. Your idea is now option d: guards keep blocking, and the guard log is read on a schedule. Each refusal is already written to the guard log (lint/guard_log_report.py reads it), so the new part is a named reader, which is triage at each roadmap review. One gap: in a cloud session that report reads n/a, so I have not measured where a cloud container's log lives. Pick d, or another option.

title: Should a new guard first run in a log-only stage before it blocks, as the Claude Code team does?
why: d is your idea: guards keep blocking, and a named reader checks the log, which fits the rule that a log needs a reader and costs no new process; b holds a new guard back. Recommended by triage, not owner-typed.
